title: Solo infra shift — quicknotes and checklist
content:
Shift start: quick brain dump & checklist (things I want at hand)

Today: morning solo shift (handed off at 06:45 PST). Main focus: GPU pool capacity + edge NIC flaps we saw last night. Keep this as my scratchpad — quick commands, thresholds, todo items, and notes to self.

Top-of-shift checks (10m)
- [ ] Check incident channel & high-priority threads (slack: #infra-ops) — any new alerts since last handoff
- [ ] GPU pool health: dashboard -> https://dash.internal/redwood/gpu-pool (watch: free_gpus, avg_queue_ms)
  - thresholds: free_gpus < 6 -> consider scale-up; avg_queue_ms > 200ms -> inspect batching/backpressure
- [ ] Network: edge router (arnold-router-1) status — any BGP flaps last 6h
  - quick command: ssh ops@bastion && ./scripts/check-bgp.sh arnold-router-1
- [ ] KMS/HSM health: rotate jobs completed? (quick check in /ops/keys)
- [ ] Scheduled maintenance windows: none for today (double-check calendar)

Useful commands (copy/paste)
- GPU pool nodes: kubectl get nodes -l role=gpu -o wide  # check Ready/NotReady
- Pods on problematic nodes: kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
- Restart pod (safe): kubectl rollout restart deployment/<deployment> -n dedicated
- Check ASG sizes (aws): aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --query 'AutoScalingGroups[?contains(Tags[].Value, `gpu-pool`)]'
- Quick spot termination check: aws ec2 describe-instance-status --instance-ids <id> --include-all-instances

Network-specific checklist (edge NIC flaps)
- Symptom: observed ARP storms and dropped connections on arnold-router-1 between 02:00-03:30 UTC.
- First triage: check edge router and switch counters, confirm if it’s a single topology or wide-spread.
- If BGP session flapping -> check peer logs, verify MTU mismatch or interface errors
- If ASIC/port error -> escalate to networking: @Jordan (ping via slack) and open INFRA-NET Jira if not already created (JIRA:INFRA-???).

GPU eviction / capacity emergency flow (fast path)
- Trigger: >10% running pods in Pending due to InsufficientGPU OR spot eviction rate spikes > 2/hr
- Immediate actions:
  1) Scale up reserved pool: ./ops/scale-gpu-reserved.sh +2 (this uses the reserved-capacity ASG)
  2) Failover routing: route small-burst jobs to dedicated-burst cluster (see runbook link in linked_artifacts)
  3) Reprioritize lower-tier batch jobs (label batch=true) -> cordon nodes used by batch jobs and evict carefully
- Postmortem: add event to JIRA INFRA-842 and tag with affected customers

Notes to self: quick debugging snippets
- Check KV cache hit rate for prefix caching: curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/kvcache | jq '.hit_rate'
- If cache miss storm, try warming with top-100 prompt prefixes (script: ops/cache-warmup/top-100)
- For model-serving runtime OOMs, check logs at /var/log/serving/runtime and grep for "OOM". Example: sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -n 200 | grep -i oom

Open todos (personal)
- [ ] Finish pruning old monitoring alerts (lots of noisy GPU mem warnings) — follow up with observability team (Samira). (Jira: OBS-301)
- [ ] Update the private runbook: add the scale-up + fallback steps I used last month (copy into confluence under infra/runbooks)
- [ ] Test the new autoscaler behavior in staging (cluster: staging-gpu-2) — create a cheap load test to verify burst scaling doesn't overshoot
- [ ] Sweep: confirm we are using the quantized model profiles on dedicated-burst; if not, coordinate with model-onboarding

Random scratch / brainstorming (do later)
- Could we add a tiny pre-warm step for ephemeral spot nodes at boot that pins model shards for 2 minutes? Might reduce tail latency on first requests. Note: needs kernel preloading and testing on Ampere/MI300 variants.
- Idea: add per-tenant soft cap so a single team doesn’t starve the pool during spike windows. Would need priority queues + billing hooks.

Escalation contacts (quick)
- Networking: Jordan Patel (slack), pager (oncall-net)
- SRE/Runtime: Samira O'Neill (slack), phone (gold)
- Platform lead: @Marta Ruiz (for cross-team change approvals)

End-of-shift handoff notes (what to write at end)
- What I observed/alerts seen
- Actions taken and commands ran (paste history)
- State of capacity (free_gpus, queued_ms), any follow-ups and who owns them

Sticker: keep this concise during the shift. When there's time, copy the useful bits into the formal runbook and link here.

-- Ava
